lines.beaver: 민호 씨, 무슨 고민 있어요? 표정이 안 좋네요.
lines.beaver_en: Minho, is something bothering you? You look down.
lines.beaver_roman: Minho ssi, museun gomin isseoyo? Pyojeongi an jonneyo.
lines.en: Could I ask you about honorific language?

lines.beaver_en: Of course. What do you want to know?
lines.en: What kind of speech do I use with elders?

lines.beaver_en: Use polite speech. Add 'yo' at the end.
lines.en: Is it the same when asking Grandma how she is?

lines.beaver_en: Yes, just say "Have you been well?"
lines.learner: 절은 언제 하나요? 매일 하는 건가요?
lines.en: When do you do a deep bow? Every day?
lines.roman: Jeoreun eonje hanayo? Maeil haneun geongayo?

lines.beaver_en: No, you do it on holidays.
lines.en: Is the big New Year's greeting a deep bow?

lines.beaver_en: Right. Do you know public etiquette too?
lines.en: Is giving up your seat on the subway good manners?

lines.beaver_en: Yes, it's nice to give it to older people.
lines.learner: 버스가 붐빌 때도 꼭 그래야 하나요?
lines.en: Even when the bus is crowded?
lines.roman: Beoseuga bumbil ttaedo kkok geuraeya hanayo?

lines.beaver_en: Of course. Anything else you're curious about?
lines.en: When do you say 'Not at all'?

lines.beaver: 누가 고맙다고 할 때 하는 말이에요.
lines.beaver_en: You say it when someone thanks you.
lines.beaver_roman: Nuga gomaptago hal ttae haneun marieyo.
lines.en: Is honorific speech always this hard?

lines.beaver: 처음엔 다 그래요. 궁금하면 또 물어봐요.
lines.beaver_en: Everyone feels that way at first. Ask me again anytime.
lines.beaver_roman: Cheoeumen da geuraeyo. Gunggeumhamyeon tto mureobwayo.
lines.en: Thank you. I feel relieved now.
